design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (excess_flood_layering, env_0065).

[0] Draw (skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0065_flood_insurance_carrier/tasks/excess_flood_layering --task 0): {"task": 0, "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 6]}. Root excess_ext_limit_increase_premium takes 6 factors, prerequisite excess_ext_renewal_term_premium takes 6.

[1] Why this is a good test. Malcolm Rutledge asks only for his excess building coverage to be raised as high as the policy allows, today. The agent must (a) see from the records that the policy record still carries the 2025-10-01..2026-10-01 term although a full payment for the 2026-10-01 term (2,061.70, posted 2026-08-28) and in-force underlying declarations (NFIP 4400918275 to 2027-05-15) are on file, (b) read in the increase rule that the additional premium is figured only once the record carries the term in which the increase takes effect, (c) work out from the renewal rule that booking the paid renewal is the one write that puts that term on the record, (d) rate the renewal with six adjustments read from the excess ledger and from the customer's Tidemark NFIP Dwelling Form records, and (e) price the to-value increase on the renewed term with six more adjustments. Difficulty comes from reading policy, reconciling a 24-row premium ledger, nine NFIP claim rows, two NFIP certificates, seven NFIP renewal bills and a 52-row NFIP premium ledger, and calculating — not from tool choice (each problem has one hidden tool).

[2] Scope snapshot. Occupied before task 0: nothing. Claimed by task 0: excess_ext_renewal_term_premium (book_excess_renewal_30706efc, agent) and excess_ext_limit_increase_premium (sign_excess_limit_increase_cddf0413, user). Left for task 1 (draw [6,5], one prerequisite): the insured's cancellation on a sale and the excess loss-of-use payment (excess_policy_cancelled / excess_premium_credit / excess_refund_disbursed and excess_claim_paid), which share no tool, event or factor with task 0.

[3] Problem-tree card. Root P_INC = excess_ext_limit_increase_premium (owner=user tool). Edge P_INC -> P_REN (excess_ext_renewal_term_premium), kind value_input, gate charged_share (also layer_rate via the booked term premium), form state. Prerequisite sentence (affirmative direction, as a pricing desk states a charge that rests on a term): "The additional premium for a limit increase is figured only once the policy record carries the term in which the increase takes effect, from that term's start to its end." Four-point test: ordering connective "only once"; waits on a record-visible state (term_start/term_end on the policy record and the term's booked items); names no tool, id or code token; hard requirement at the exact scope (the term containing the increase's effective date). Exactly one write of the difficulty sets a policy record's term: the renewal booking (the increase writes limits/term premium, the task-1 tools write cancellation fields and claim rows). Derivation: sentence + record (term ends 2026-10-01, payment for 2026-10-01 term on file, evidence in force) + renewal rule ("is booked as the next term, starting on the day the current term ends") -> book the renewal. Opening falsity: excess_policies.term_start=2025-10-01, term_end=2026-10-01; no TERM_PREMIUM item for 2026-10-01. Resolution order [P_REN, P_INC]. Deletion sensitivity (harness run): skipping the renewal makes the increase recompute to 0.00 (term on record ended 2026-10-01: the waiting period would end after the term end, so the share on that term is nothing and the increase belongs to the next term) instead of 175.93. The persona never names the renewal; tools validate no prerequisite.

[4] Base-invariant card. Step 12 (excess_term_renewed): excess_agg_underlying_requirement.underlying_in_force_on_term_start — declarations received 2026-05-20 (excess_changes) show 4400918275 in force 2026-05-15..2027-05-15, covering the 2026-10-01 term start; bound to the tool argument underlying_policy_number. excess_renewal (policy_scope): full payment received 2026-08-28 <= term_end 2026-10-01, evidence received 2026-05-20; no grace issue. excess_premium_rating (policy_scope, its premium sentence retired for renewals by declared overwrite). Step 14 (excess_endorsement_issued): excess_endorsements.endorsable_status — status active; excess_limits_eligibility — 250,000 + 1,450,000 = 1,700,000 <= 100 percent of RCV 1,700,000, 2M tier range 1,050,000..2,000,000, multiple of 50,000, zone AE needs no certificate on 2M; excess_waiting_period — its increase sentence retired for to-value increases by declared overwrite (flat as of term start inside the first 30 days when no claim on the policy has a date of loss on or after the term start). No time-kind eligibility applies to either write.

[5] Business-object card. Target: Excess Flood policy EXF-4410382 (one policy on the profile). Renewal object: the 2026-10-01 term, keyed by term_start on the payment row; earlier terms (2021..2025) and the 2026-02-10 stated-limit increase items are excluded by term_start/charge_basis. Increase object: the excess dwelling limit of that policy; the endorsement row the tool writes carries the policy id and its items reference the endorsement id.

[6] Factor card — renewal (6). baseline (computation document): scheduled layer x zone factor x elevation multiplier (excess record only) + loss-of-use charge, rounded, min 1,450 -> 1,795.00 (= the renewal offer, a decoy). Factors (tier taken / evidence / result with that factor at baseline): renewal_loss_history param, multi-source (layer payments x primary payments of the NFIP/HomeFlood policy of the home) — one NFIP building payment 2024-11-20, no layer payment -> +10; the 2023-09-28 payment (36 whole months) and the same-day contents payment are near-misses / 1450.00. tidemark_account_relationship param — no active HomeFlood, NFIP in force -> -4 / 1557.25. residence_designation param — NFIP primary_residence true -> -3 / 1543.78. tenure_on_layer param — 4 RENEWAL term premiums -> -3 / 1543.78. payment_ahead_of_term_end param — payment for the 2026-10-01 term posted 34 days ahead -> -4 / 1557.25. certificate_source method — no certificate on the excess record; latest applied certificate of the NFIP policy of the home 14.6 - 12.0 = 2.6 ft -> 0.85 (unapplied 2012 certificate not read) / 1731.60. Result 1,503.36; all-baseline 1,795.00. Cross-difficulty: four factors read the dwelling category, only through the NFIP policy of the home (address + in force).

[7] Factor card — increase (6). baseline: added limit/1000 x (booked term premium - loss-of-use charge)/(limit/1000) x (days left - 30)/term days -> 182.56. Factors: signing_window method — signed 13 days after the 2026-10-01 term start, no claim on the policy -> flat, share 1 / 155.20. rate_derivation method — booked 1503.36 above minimum with excess personal property -> dwelling share 1375/1585 of (1503.36 - 210) over 1250 = 0.8976 / 202.80. layer_position param — 250,000 + 1,250,000 = 1,500,000 -> 0.8 (inclusive boundary) / 219.91. primary_loss_recency param — 22 months -> +10 / 161.57. repeat_increase param — one increase 2026-02-10 -> +7.5 / 165.16. zone_of_record_surcharge param — NFIP zone AE -> +5 / 168.75. Result 175.93; revised full-term premium 1,679.29.

[8] Factor independence table (mechanical, transitive): renewal — loss_history reads primary_paid_recent, layer_paid_recent; account reads homeflood_primary_active, nfip_primary_in_force; residence reads nfip_primary_residence; tenure reads renewals_booked; payment_ahead reads renewal_paid_on, days_paid_ahead; certificate_source reads nfip_cert_* and the record — no factor binding reads another factor's binding; assembly only in net_adjust_pct/adjusted_layer/result. Increase — signing_window reads days_*; rate_derivation reads booked_term_premium and plain rates/zone; layer_position reads underlying_dwelling_limit; recency reads last_primary_payment; repeat reads increases_recent; zone surcharge reads nfip_zone/zone_read; assembly in increase_loading_pct/full_term_charge/result.

[9] Method tier pairwise table. certificate_source: (record cert) vs (NFIP cert) differ when ec_on_file flips; (NFIP cert) vs (none) differ when an applied NFIP certificate exists; (record) vs (none) differ by ec_on_file. signing_window: flat vs waiting-period share (floored at 60 days) differ by days into term (<=30 vs >30) or a claim in the term; flat vs nothing differ by days into term (13 vs 335 or more days in); waiting-period share vs nothing differ by days left (more than 30 vs 30 or fewer, where the waiting period ends on or after the term end). rate_derivation: minimum vs share differ by booked premium (<=1450 vs >1450); share vs plain differ by excess contents limit (>0 vs 0); minimum vs plain differ by booked premium.

[10] Edge probes (scratch copies, harness): absent NFIP record -> account 0, occupancy 0, zone falls back to record zone, loss/recency count 0 (tier covers absent case); a cancelled HomeFlood at the address -> EXISTS(... status='active') false; second dwelling certificate unapplied -> filtered by ec_applied; renewal payment missing -> days_paid_ahead 0 tier; elevation_difference_ft empty with ec_on_file false never compared; increase signed before term start -> days_into_term < 0 falls to the waiting tier; booked term premium at minimum -> schedule-rate tier.

[11] Persona. Courteous retired harbor pilot; volunteers only the goal ("as high as your excess policy will allow ... done today"), authorizes servicing, signs himself; identity (phone, SSN last four, then ZIP/email) only on request; passive facts on request: primary residence, NFIP with Tidemark, certificate with the federal policy, 2023/2024 NFIP claims, February increase, renewal paid by bank draft in late August. Ends after the increase is confirmed; no extra asks.

[12] Standard solution. Locate (phone), verify (phone + 4318), read excess policy, billing, changes, claims, NFIP policy/claims/changes/billing, HomeFlood (none). Book renewal: term_premium 1503.36, underlying 4400918275 -> credit 309.14 remains. Hand over the increase: new limit 1,450,000, effective 2026-10-01, additional 175.93, revised 1679.29; tool books 10.56 tax; credit after: 122.65.

[13] Verification. Harness (scratch, replays gold with the real tools and evaluates compute through check_compute.build_env/eval_compute): renewal 1503.36 with sensitivity {renewal_loss_history 1450, tidemark_account_relationship 1557.25, residence_designation 1543.78, tenure_on_layer 1543.78, payment_ahead_of_term_end 1557.25, certificate_source 1731.6, all-baseline 1795.0}; increase 175.93 with {signing_window 155.2, rate_derivation 202.8, layer_position 219.91, primary_loss_recency 161.57, repeat_increase 165.16, zone_of_record_surcharge 168.75, all-baseline 182.56}; increase without the renewal 0.0. No half-cent tie (1293.36 + 210; 175.9296).

[14] Draft recomputation from the visible context: the KB will carry the increase rule (state sentence, to-value limit, flat window, rate methods, relativity, surcharges) and the renewal rule; records give every input; the same two writes and figures follow. Revisions: (r1) increase scoped to to-value requests because a computation cannot read a stated limit; the February history increase is a stated-limit increase under the base endorsement rule (re-rated 1795.00, 191.88 + 11.51 tax). (r2) flat window bounded below by the term start.

REWORK round 2: loss-history ladder made realistic and multi-source (a layer payment or two primary payments -> 25 %, exactly one primary payment and no layer payment -> 10 %); every NFIP read confined to the NFIP policy of the home (address + in force); certificate reads filtered to that policy; flat window requires no claim with a date of loss on or after the term start; prerequisite sentence states the term end as excluded; condition no longer adds the booked item; renewal payment date moved to 2026-08-28 to remove the half-cent tie (early-renewal tier now 30 days or more); persona's servicing line made neutral and payment month updated.
REWORK round 4 (renderer source scan): increase window's short-term tier is now a 60-day minimum share (reachable once the record carries the term); scheduled charges defined in the increase rule; absent underlying declarations or booked term premium fall back to the policy record; certificate age stated in whole months; every overwrite tail restates the base content it keeps for other cases; loss-history counts net of voided payments; single-factor bindings moved into their factors; same-day tie-break stated. Task 0 scored values unchanged; renewal-skip sensitivity now 35.44 (superseded in round 5: 0.00).
REWORK round 5: the short-term tier was narrowed to 59 days left down to the boundary (see round 6); with fewer days the waiting share is nothing and the increase belongs to the next term, matching the prerequisite sentence; loss-history voids are stated as counted by the void's own date in the window; tie-break sentence also covers two policy records answering the same description. Scored values unchanged; renewal-skip sensitivity back to 0.00.
REWORK round 6: the short-term tier is now 'more than 30 but fewer than 60 days of the term remain' (31 to 59 days); at exactly 30 days left the waiting period ends on the term end, so the increase belongs to the next term and the share is nothing, agreeing with the prerequisite's 'up to, but not including, its end' (probed at 29/30/31 days left: nothing, nothing, the 60-day minimum share). Every read of a policy that a second record of the same kind could answer is now keyed by its identifying value: the NFIP and HomeFlood policies of the home by the underlying policy number on the policy record (account, occupancy, loss history, certificate, primary-loss recency, flood zone), the underlying declarations by the underlying policy number, the booked term premium by the current term start (latest item). Decoy probes (a second in-force NFIP policy on the same address with another number, its own recent building payment, later declarations for another underlying number) leave both results unchanged; no scored value moved.
REWORK round 8: the 60-day minimum is now a real floor: every non-flat increase whose waiting period ends before the term end is charged the share from the end of the waiting period, never less than 60 days over the days of the term; where the waiting period ends on or after the term end nothing is charged (rule, ladder and compute identical). Probed at 29/30/31/59/60/61/89/90/91/120 days left: nothing, nothing, then 60 days charged through 90 days left, 61 at 91, 90 at 120 - the charge never falls as the remaining term grows. Task 0 takes the flat tier; no scored value moved.
REWORK round 10 (seed only; charter and tools byte-identical): the NFIP Dwelling Form record now carries the history its published rules write. Premium ledger, one term per year from new business 2019-05-15: risk and ICC premiums as rated (2,240/75, 2,310/75, then 1,655 to 1,842 with ICC 63 after the certificate, each renewal within the 18 percent cap), Reserve Fund Assessment 18 percent of risk plus ICC, HFIAA 25 (primary residence on a tier that carries the lower surcharge), Federal Policy Fee 50, each term paid in full by escrow disbursement before the term end. The 2021-03-02 certificate re-rated the 2020-05-15 term to 1,620/63 (lower, so applied): re-rate credits 139.89 risk, 2.43 ICC and 25.62 Reserve Fund Assessment for the 74 of 365 days left, refunded to the lender's escrow as payor of record; the 2019 certificate re-rated higher (2,295/75) and stays on file unapplied. Renewal bills issued 45 days before each expiration carry the indicated risk premium booked. A gold read of the NFIP ledger (step 9) covers the new rows, shifting the writes to steps 12 and 14. No compute reads these rows; no scored value moved.
user_scenario:
You are Malcolm Rutledge, a retired harbor pilot in your late sixties who lives year-round with your wife in the house at 418 Surfsong Rd, Kiawah Island, SC 29455. You speak in an unhurried, courteous Lowcountry way, a little formal, and you like to get things settled in one call. Tidemark carries both your federal flood policy and an Excess Flood policy on the house. You are calling because you want the excess building coverage on that house raised as high as your excess policy will allow, and you want it done today; you are not asking for a quote to think about. You do not know or name a dollar figure for the new limit — when the agent asks how much, you say you want it as high as the policy lets you go on that house. You are happy for the agent to look at your records and handle your account as Tidemark's rules require, and you understand you will sign the limit change yourself.

You give your details only when the agent asks for them, one or two at a time: your phone number is 8435541274, and the last four of your Social Security number are 4318. If a further detail is needed, your ZIP code is 29455 and your email is malcolm.rutledge@gmail.com. If the agent asks for a policy number, you say you don't have the paperwork in front of you and ask them to look it up by your name or phone.

Only if the agent asks, you can say: the house is your primary residence and you live there all year; the federal flood policy on it is also with Tidemark; you think there is an elevation certificate on file with that federal policy; you had water in the garage in the summer of 2024 and the federal policy paid that claim, there was also a smaller federal claim after a king tide in late August 2023, and the excess policy has never paid you anything; you raised the excess coverage once before, back in February. If the agent asks about your renewal, you say you paid what the renewal notice asked for, by bank draft, in late August, though you don't remember the exact amount — something a little over two thousand dollars. You don't know anything about rates, credits or how the premium is worked out, and you don't offer opinions on them.

When the agent tells you what the increase will cost and how it will be paid, you accept it as the agent explains it; if the agent tells you a credit already on your account covers it, you say that's fine with you. When the agent hands you the limit change to sign, you sign it using exactly the figures and dates the agent gives you, and you read the confirmation back if asked. Once the agent tells you the increase has been recorded, you thank them and end the call. If the agent tells you the increase cannot be done, you ask them to explain why in one sentence, thank them and end the call.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.new_excess_building_limit: (1) 1450000. (2) Rule of the increase policy: 'The new excess dwelling limit is the highest whole multiple of the tier's limit increment for which the building attachment point plus that limit stays within the tier's maximum percentage of the replacement cost value on the policy record, and never above the tier's maximum excess dwelling limit'; the customer asks for the limit 'as high as the policy lets you go on that house'. (3) RCV 1,700,000 x 100% - attachment 250,000 = 1,450,000, a whole multiple of 50,000 and below the 2M tier maximum of 2,000,000; 1,500,000 would put attachment plus limit at 1,750,000 > 1,700,000, so no larger limit qualifies and the customer asked for no smaller one.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.change_effective_date: (1) 2026-10-01. (2) Rule: 'the increase takes effect as of the term start when it is signed on or after the term start and no more than 30 days after it with no claim on the policy having a date of loss on or after the term start'. (3) After the renewal the term starts 2026-10-01; the increase is signed 2026-10-14, 13 days in, and the excess claim file is empty, so the term start is the only date the rule gives; a 30-day wait applies only outside that window.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.additional_premium: 175.93. Added limit 1,450,000 - 1,250,000 = 200,000. Layer rate: booked 2026-10-01 term premium 1503.36 is above the 1,450 minimum and the policy carries excess personal property, so rate = (1503.36 - 210) x (1375/1585) / 1250 = 0.8976 per 1,000. Layer relativity 0.8 (dwelling limit 250,000 on the 2026-05-20 declarations + excess limit 1,250,000 = 1,500,000, at least 1,500,000). Increase loading = 10 (latest payment on the NFIP policy of the home 2024-11-20, 22 whole months before) + 7.5 (one limit increase recorded 2026-02-10 within 12 months) + 5 (NFIP zone AE) = 22.5. Full-term charge 200 x 0.8976 x 0.8 x 1.225 = 175.9296; charged share 1 (signed 13 days after the term start, no claim) -> 175.93.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.revised_term_premium: (1) 1679.29. (2) Rule: 'The full-term premium as endorsed is the term premium before the increase plus the additional premium before the charged share of the term is applied, rounded to the cent.' (3) 1503.36 + 175.9296 = 1679.2896 -> 1679.29.

edges.condition: excess_policies.term_start is on or before the date the increase takes effect and excess_policies.term_end is after it.
edges.policy_source: The additional premium for a limit increase is figured only once the policy record carries the term in which the increase takes effect, from that term's start up to, but not including, its end.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: On 2026-10-14 the policy record still carries the term 2025-10-01..2026-10-01; an increase signed that day takes effect on or after 2026-10-01 (term start of the paid renewal, or 2026-11-13 after a 30-day wait), outside the recorded term, and no TERM_PREMIUM item for the 2026-10-01 term stands on the account.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The renewal booking sets term_start 2026-10-01, term_end 2027-10-01, term_premium 1503.36 and books the 2026-10-01 TERM_PREMIUM item; the increase then takes effect inside the recorded term.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A single edge: the increase depends on the renewal and nothing depends on the increase; there is no parallel prerequisite to reorder. Writing the increase first would figure it on the ended 2025-10-01 term, where the waiting period ends after the term end and the share is nothing (0.00), and leave the renewal unbooked.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the renewal leaves the record on the 2025-10-01..2026-10-01 term: the waiting period would end after the term end, so the share on that term is nothing and the additional premium recomputes to 0.00 instead of 175.93; the policy also keeps term_end 2026-10-01 and no 2026-10-01 renewal items, a different terminal state.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario never mentions the renewal booking, the term on record or any servicing step; the only renewal fact is a passive answer ('If the agent asks about your renewal, you say you paid what the renewal notice asked for') given only on the agent's question, and it states the payment, not that anything is unbooked.
